about: The legacy read parity matrix. One row per query shape, executed on both
the legacy and experimental Cypher engines against a shared fixture graph.
Expected values are recorded, never inferred at run time: a disagreement
between the two engines is a finding, not a file to update.

bookmarks.statement: Bookmark behaviour is not a per-shape property in this tree. Bookmarks live at the client service layer (src/client/service.rs:401-462); a QueryContext carries read_epoch but nothing bookmark-shaped reaches the shard, so every read shape would record an identical value. Recorded once here for all read shapes, with a per-row read_epoch and storage_sequence expectation instead.

rows.query: MATCH (e:Entity) WHERE e.entity_id = $id RETURN e.entity_id AS id, e.rank AS rank ORDER BY id ASC
MATCH (e:Entity) WHERE e.entity_id = $left OR e.entity_id = $right RETURN e.entity_id AS id, e.rank AS rank ORDER BY rank DESC, id ASC
MATCH (a:Entity)-[:KNOWS]->(b:Person) WHERE a.entity_id = $id RETURN b.name AS name
MATCH (e:Entity) WHERE e.entity_id STARTS WITH '' RETURN e.entity_id AS id ORDER BY e.entity_id DESC LIMIT 2
MATCH (e:Entity) RETURN e.entity_id AS id ORDER BY id ASC
MATCH (e:Entity {id: $id}) RETURN e.entity_id AS id
MATCH (e:Entity) RETURN e.entity_id AS id ORDER BY id ASC SKIP 1 LIMIT 1
MATCH (e:Entity) RETURN *

divergence.reason: Legacy refuses star projections. The engine spells the star out as every name the query wrote that is in scope, in name order -- Neo4j's column order -- followed by any items after it. The recorded rows are Neo4j's answer, checked by hand; `just neo4j-oracle` holds them to Neo4j. Public error class on legacy unchanged: query.

rows.query: MATCH (a:Entity)-[:KNOWS*1..2]-(b:Person) WHERE a.entity_id = $id RETURN b.name AS name

divergence.reason: Legacy refuses variable-length undirected relationships. The semantics this row's earlier scope exclusion called undefined are Neo4j's, which the oracle now pins: one traversal over both orientations, trail semantics keyed on relationship identity -- a self-loop is one step, each edge of a reciprocal pair is its own path, and a path may return to its start over different relationships. The recorded rows are Neo4j's answer, checked by hand; `just neo4j-oracle` holds them to Neo4j. Public error class on legacy unchanged: query.

rows.query: MATCH (e:Entity) WITH e RETURN e.entity_id AS id ORDER BY id ASC
MATCH (e:Entity) WITH e.entity_id AS id RETURN id ORDER BY id ASC

divergence.reason: Legacy's WITH is a validated no-op that rejects aliases, DISTINCT, WHERE, ORDER BY, SKIP and LIMIT (src/query/opencypher.rs:2891-2939), so there is no legacy behaviour for these shapes to be identical to. an internal tracking item Workstream 8 implements WITH as a real scope boundary, which the definition of done permits where the new engine intentionally adds support and carries a positive correctness test. The recorded rows above are that test; legacy's refusal is pinned by error_class.

divergence.reason: legacy refuses count(n) while answering count(*) on the same scan -- it reads the binding inside count() as a property-value expression and reports that property values support only integer, float, boolean and string literals. The engine counts the binding and returns the same total. count(n) is ordinary openCypher, so this is a legacy gap the engine declines to reproduce, not a deliberate difference. The recorded row is the positive correctness test the definition of done requires. Public error class unchanged: query.

divergence.reason: Legacy's WITH accepts only pass-through identifiers. The engine groups at a WITH boundary exactly as RETURN groups, carrying a grouping key that is a node across as a node; what follows reads the grouped rows. The recorded rows are Neo4j's answer, checked by hand; `just neo4j-oracle` holds them to Neo4j. Public error class on legacy unchanged: query.

rows.query: MATCH (e:Entity) WITH e.score AS n MATCH (n:Tag) RETURN n.name AS name ORDER BY name ASC

neo4j.reason: Neo4j also refuses: n is a value, and a pattern cannot rebind it as a node (type mismatch, Neo.ClientError.Statement.SyntaxError). The refusal is the specified behaviour, not a gap.

rows.query: MATCH (e:Entity) WITH e.score AS n MATCH (t:Tag) WHERE n > 0 RETURN t.name AS name ORDER BY name ASC

divergence.reason: legacy refuses any WITH that is not a bare pass-through; the engine treats WITH as a projection boundary, so a value it computed can be read by a later predicate. Reading such a name is allowed and binding it is not -- see combo_with_value_bound_as_node, which both routes refuse. Net-new capability with a recorded correctness test. Public error class on legacy unchanged: query.

rows.query: MATCH (e:Entity) WITH e AS x MATCH (x)-[:TAGGED]->(t:Tag) RETURN t.name AS name ORDER BY name ASC

divergence.reason: legacy refuses WITH aliases outright; the engine carries the binding through under its new name, so a later pattern may expand from it. Renaming a binding keeps it a graph element, unlike projecting a property off it. Net-new capability with a recorded correctness test. Public error class on legacy unchanged: query.

rows.query: MATCH (e:Entity) WITH e.score AS n WITH n AS x MATCH (x:Tag) RETURN x.name AS name ORDER BY name ASC

neo4j.reason: Neo4j also refuses: x carries the value n held, and a pattern cannot rebind it as a node (type mismatch, Neo.ClientError.Statement.SyntaxError). The refusal is the specified behaviour, not a gap.

rows.query: MATCH (a:Entity) OPTIONAL MATCH (a)-[:MISSING]->(p) WITH p MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name ORDER BY name ASC

divergence.reason: legacy refuses this WITH form outright. The engine answers it, and the answer is the empty set: an OPTIONAL that matched nothing binds the name to null, a null binding matches no pattern, so the following MATCH eliminates every row. That emptiness is the whole point of the row -- before the fix this returned nine rows, three entities crossed with three people, because the projection carried the null across the boundary as a value and dropped the null binding, and the pattern then scanned. Compare combo_optional_null_read_through_with, where the same null is read rather than bound and both routes answer three nulls.

exclusion.reason: An UNWIND batch, claimed by the client service layer above the shard (parse_opencypher_unwind_batch), so it never reaches either Cypher engine and there is no engine-versus-engine comparison to make.
